Scenario Compass Evaluation

Source: vignettes/Scenario_Compass_Evaluation.Rmd
Scenario_Compass_Evaluation.Rmd

The Scenario Compass Initiative is a community-driven framework designed to continuously collect, curate, and assess global emissions scenarios. It provides a robust infrastructure for transparently vetting modeled pathways against real-world historical data and updated feasibility benchmarks.

In gcamreport, we have streamlined the process of evaluating your model runs. By bridging our standardization workflow directly with the Scenario Compass criteria, you can instantly assess how your scenarios measure up!

This functionality is powered by the scenariocompass_checker() function. You can run it as a standalone tool, or trigger it automatically while standardizing your data via the generate_report() function.

newline

Before we begin: For the examples presented here, we assume you already have gcamreport installed and know the basics. If you are new here, check out our Step-by-Step Tutorial first.

Note: This process saves a .csv evaluation file in the same folder as the standardized data. You can also view the results directly in the console

newline

Example 1: standardize and evaluate an entire dataset

Suppose you have a project file (or analogously, a database) that you wish to standardize and evaluate. To evaluate all the regions and scenarios contained within, you can indicate it as follows:

generate_report(
  prj_name = 'path/to/project/name', 
  GCAM_version = 'your_GCAM_version',
  scenariocompass_evaluation = TRUE
)

newline

Example 2: evaluate a GCAM run agains SCI criteria

Suppose your primary objective is to assess whether a GCAM run complies with the Scenario Compass criteria. You can optimize the process by restricting standardization exclusively to the variables required for the assessment.

generate_report(
  prj_name = 'path/to/project/name', 
  GCAM_version = 'your_GCAM_version',
  scenariocompass_evaluation = TRUE,
  desired_variables = 'SCI'
)

newline

Example 3: evaluate only the global or the regional criteria

Suppose you want to evaluate a GCAM run against specific Scenario Compass thresholds; whether (a) global criteria, (b) broad regional criteria, or (c) criteria for a specific country or region present in your GCAM version. You can easily tailor the assessment by defining the regional scope. If no scope is specified (the default setting), the tool will automatically perform both the global and the standard regional evaluations.

# To evaluate against global criteria only:
generate_report(
  prj_name = 'path/to/project/name', 
  GCAM_version = 'your_GCAM_version',
  scenariocompass_evaluation = TRUE,
  scenariocompass_regions = 'World'
)
                
# To evaluate against regional criteria only:
generate_report(
  prj_name = 'path/to/project/name', 
  GCAM_version = 'your_GCAM_version',
  scenariocompass_evaluation = TRUE,
  scenariocompass_regions = 'Regional'
)

# To evaluate against a certain region/country (e.g., USA and China) criteria only:
generate_report(
  prj_name = 'path/to/project/name', 
  GCAM_version = 'your_GCAM_version',
  scenariocompass_evaluation = TRUE,
  scenariocompass_regions = c('USA','China')
)

newline

Example 4: evaluate targeted scenarios

Suppose you have multiple GCAM runs and, although you wish to standardize them all, you only want a subset to be assessed. You can specify the target scenarios for evaluation. If nothing is indicated (default), all scenarios will be evaluated

generate_report(prj_name = 'path/to/project/name', 
                GCAM_version = 'your_GCAM_version',
                scenariocompass_evaluation = TRUE,
                scenariocompass_scenarios = c('scen1','scen2'))

newline

Example 5: evaluate an already standardized dataset

Suppose you have previous GCAM runs that are already standardized. You can assess them against the Scenario Compass criteria directly by loading the standardized RData, .csv or .xlsx file.

scenariocompass_checker(
  report = 'path/to/standardized/dataset.RData', # also accepts .csv or .xlsx
  GCAM_version = 'your_GCAM_version'
)
